predecessors.name: Later Yan
predecessors.text: Huatai (modern Hua County, Henan), where Murong De took the title Prince of Yan in 398

successors.name: Jin dynasty (Western and Eastern Jin)
successors.text: the Southern Yan's Shandong, Cliopatria's 407-409 shape

ledger.x: 398: Murong De founds the Southern Yan at Huatai.
399: Huatai falls to the Northern Wei.
399: De takes Qing Province from Eastern Jin and sets up at Guanggu.
399: the capital moves from Huatai to Guanggu; De takes the title Emperor of Yan in 400.
409: Liu Yu marches on the Southern Yan.
410: Liu Yu ends the Southern Yan.

wars.name: Murong De's secession from Later Yan
wars.outcome: De split from Later Yan at Huatai and nearly captured Murong Bao there; the Later Yan dossier records Bao's assassination the same year.

wars.name: Northern Wei capture of Huatai
wars.outcome: A traitor opens Huatai's gates to Wei forces; De moves on to Qing Province.

wars.name: Murong De's conquest of Qing Province
wars.outcome: De seizes Qing Province from Eastern Jin and establishes Guanggu in modern central and eastern Shandong; Jin exiles later move in during Huan Xuan's rebellion.

wars.name: Liu Yu's campaign against the Southern Yan
wars.outcome: Liu Yu wins at Linqu and besieges Guanggu; the city falls in 410, Chao is executed and the Jin annex the state; Later Qin, fighting Helian Xia, sends no relief.

certainty.note: The pages give only the Qing Province / central and eastern Shandong and Huatai; no frontier with the Jin or the Wei is given.
